extracted_by: hand, T-0261 — the Chicago American read, June to August 1835
note: Volume I, Number 1: the American's own first issue. Pages 1, 2 and most of 4 are reprinted eastern and British matter with no Chicago content; the town is in page 3 columns 3 to 6. The masthead ('CHICAGO AMERICAN. / BY T. O. DAVIS.') sits in the transcription's FRONT MATTER, before the first page heading, so no locator can reach it — the paper's own establishment is therefore cited from the two editorial paragraphs inside page 3 column 3 that say the same thing. This issue's page 3 column 6 is the case `locator.spans` was added for: line 409 is a single 8,024-character blob carrying four advertisements, a fifth column's text and the segmenter's own coordinate telemetry, all woven together.

claims.notes: THE PLACEMENT IS ADVERTISED AND UNREADABLE, which is why the class is `none` and not `relative`. Line 394 reads 'jisawell jn the sore behieee ee Ree' — 'himself in the store be[hind/below] …' — and whatever the store stood behind or below is destroyed by the segmenter's interleave with the adjoining column. A `relative` placement with a guessed anchor would place a storefront on nothing — and the guess would have been wrong: the next issue sets the same advertisement with the address intact, 'on Randolph [Street] over Briggs & Humphrey's' (1835-06-13 page 3 column 6 line 332), an upper floor and not a store at all. That claim carries the placement; this one carries the name. THE NAME. Only the surname is printed in the fragment that survives; 'Brown' is the whole of what the paper gives here, so it is the whole of what the gazetteer keys on.

claims.notes: WHAT THIS SHOP MAKES WAS READ WRONG HERE FIRST. 'LB, HA & TRUNK M' invites 'Hat & Trunk Manufactory'; the next issue sets the same card as 'SAPDLE. HARNESS & ... & TRUNK Macy' over the name S. B. Cobb (1835-06-13 page 3 column 6 line 335), so the heading here is '[Sadd]le, Ha[rness & Trunk] M[anufactory]' and the trade is saddlery. The correction is recorded rather than quietly applied, because the wrong reading was the plausible one and the next reader deserves to know why it is not taken. NO PROPRIETOR IS MINTED FROM THIS PRINTING: the name is not in it: it is in the second witness, and that claim mints S. B. Cobb. A CORNER, AND HALF OF IT IS READABLE: 'comer of Lake anc Amor. | stvests' gives Lake Street and a cross street; 'Amor.' matches no Chicago street name this project holds and the second printing loses the phrase entirely, so it stays inside `[uncertain: …]`. The corner class still earns its keep — the paper places this shop AT a crossing of Lake Street, which is more than `street_only`.

claims.quote: NEWBERRY & bOUJ a oy Chicago, June 8, 1835.
claims.notes: THE FIRM IS DOCUMENTED IN THE AMERICAN AND ALMOST NOTHING ELSE OF ITS ADVERTISEMENT SURVIVES the interleave — the signature line and the date are all that can be quoted, so trade, goods and address are all null. This is still worth recording: Newberry & Dole is the anchor the Democrat's Peter Cohen advertisement places a South Water Street storefront against (T-0257's fixture, claim c001), and a firm named independently in the second paper on the scene date is exactly the cross-examination this ticket exists for. NO STREET IS ASSERTED HERE: the Democrat places Cohen 'below Messrs. Newberry and Dole's' on south water street, and carrying that street across to this claim would be reading one paper into the other.

claims.notes: A DRUGGIST WITH TWELVE YEARS' EXPERIENCE, ADVERTISING IN THE AMERICAN'S FIRST ISSUE — and this blob does not yield his name. THE NAME COMES FROM THE NEXT ISSUE, NOT FROM A GUESS: 1835-06-13 page 4 column 6 lines 465-467 set the same advertisement clean — 'FREDERICK THOMAS, late of New York, has taken a store at the Drawbridge' — and the two printings share their wording sentence for sentence ('more than twelve years in the business', 'determination of strict personal attention', 'Chemicals, Perfumery and Dye Stuffs'). That is the identification, it is checkable against both quotes, and it is why the business here carries his name while the claim itself quotes only what June 8 prints. NO ADDRESS IS CARRIED ACROSS: the drawbridge anchor is in the second printing and stays on that claim. The stock list that follows in this line (Epsom Salts, quinine, Lee's Pills, eye waters, Prussian blue) is in the same unattributable condition as the Harmon, Loomis goods list and is left with it.
